# Selected alternate run branches

These 18 original DOCX files are generated by
`tools/alternate_run_recovery_fixture.py` using hand-authored XML/OPC and the
original PNG from the image-recovery generator. No third-party document engine,
font, corpus artwork, or reference-application asset is redistributed.

Nine pairs cover positions before, after and on both sides of a healthy picture,
with an understood Choice, an unknown-namespace Choice selecting Fallback, or an
empty Fallback. Each mixed run appears in the body, a table, a header and a
footer, inside a formatted hyperlink. Nonempty selected branches contain text,
a picture, a tab and more text. The matched file replaces only the wrapper with
the selected branch's contents; all surrounding content is identical.

ECMA-376 Part 3, fifth edition (2015), §§7.5–7.7 and §9 define the selection and
processing semantics. The local PDF was consulted. These controls test that
defined projection, not a claimed reference/spec divergence. There is no native reference for this recovery change. Schema validation checks the processed
standard MCE view; it is not a complete MCE conformance certificate.

Before the change, all nine unit cases lost healthy content: the single-drawing
guard escalated to a paragraph-level text approximation. Read-only import now
reads each selected item through the existing run readers. Supported text,
pictures, formatting, links and surrounding structure survive. Nested selected
branches and an unsupported ruby child have additional unit holdouts. An
unsupported selected child does not cause selection of an unselected Fallback.

Browser tests compare entire page pixels and body/story geometry to the matched
files at 100% and 75% zoom, check original-byte downloads and prevent editing.
Strict editable import still rejects these wrappers because editing and
reconstruction of arbitrary alternate run content remain unsupported. Existing
single-drawing wrappers continue through their retained-shell path. Malformed
MCE structures, broader MCE attributes, block wrappers and unrelated late
layout failures are not closed by this work.
